alternative_readings: If outside the retained HTML body means outside the main circular, the supplied document separation supports that reading. If it means absent from the joined packet, it is wrong: the packet supplies three appendix pages, Parts A and B, and both appendix footnotes. This resolves availability within the packet, not official authenticity or currentness.

Referenced legislation is more precise than incorporated legislation. Paragraphs 5–7 and 27 and footnote 7 identify statutory definitions and regimes, but do not establish incorporation of every provision of the named ordinances. Footnote 2 summarises CIS characteristics without reproducing the full statutory definition.

Non-exhaustive considerations do not establish either an exhaustive compliance safe harbour or universal technical prescriptions. Equally, their qualifications do not make the circular's due-diligence and risk-management expectations optional. The smart-contract discussion distinguishes possible audit needs from the expectation to justify reliance on a third-party audit; the secondary-record footnote preserves possible technology-audit needs.

Paragraph 18's reference to both appendix parts does not expressly erase Part B's specified bearer-form, permissionless-token and public-permissionless-network scope. Part B(f)'s omnibus-account exception concerns other customers' assets; it does not extend to the custodian's or sub-custodian's assets. Part B(j) addresses sub-custodians where their appointment is allowed, without itself granting permission.

Paragraph 26's position on a mandatory PI-only restriction remains qualified by paragraph 27's public-offering regimes and exemptions. Paragraph 24's underlying-security complexity assessment assumes effective mitigation of technology risks. Neither passage establishes unrestricted retail distribution.

Paragraph 28's treatment of the portfolio-management Terms and Conditions preserves the virtual-asset threshold condition, and paragraph 29 retains this circular's requirements. Paragraphs 30–31 contemplate a case-by-case SFC decision on compensation coverage following application and satisfactory demonstration, not an automatic exclusion. Paragraphs 32–35 retain restrictions, additional controls and notification expectations for Digital Securities; footnotes 8–9 add HKMA obligations for registered institutions.

Paragraph 21 expressly states supersession of the 2019 Statement. It does not establish that this circular remains current at a later assessment date. Background reports, headings, contact details, page labels and source-location metadata supply context or document structure, not missing legislative authority.
missing_premises: Official provenance and completeness verification linking the supplied appendix to the relevant version of 23EC52, together with publication, amendment and supersession history for the assessment date.
Official relevant-date text of SFO (Cap. 571), Schedule 1, Part 1, section 1, including the securities and relevant CIS definitions, exclusions and cross-references.

Official relevant-date operative provisions of SFO Part IV and the C(WUMP)O (Cap. 32) prospectus regime, including the precise authorisation requirements, professional-investor definitions and exemptions relied upon. The circular does not enumerate every relevant section.

Official relevant-date text of AMLO (Cap. 615), section 53ZRA, including exclusions and cross-references. Footnote 7's threshold explanation belongs to the referenced Terms and Conditions and is not a reproduction of that statutory definition.

Identification and text of the actual governing laws relevant to settlement finality, ownership, security interests, extrinsic rights and regulatory approvals. Appendix Part A raises these questions without identifying every applicable enactment or resolving them.

The separately referenced authorised-product circular, joint virtual-asset circular, portfolio-management Terms and Conditions, online-distribution guidelines, Code of Conduct, relevant complexity guidance and VATP guidelines, in their applicable versions. These regulatory dependencies must remain distinct from legislation; background BIS and GFMA reports do not fill statutory gaps.

The assessment date and facts concerning the intermediary, instrument, activity, investors, offering, authorisations or exemptions, governing law, network, token form, custody chain and any SFC decision. Supplied bytes, hashes and locators establish neither applicability nor currentness.

proposition: The appendix-content gap is resolved within the supplied joined packet: it contains a separately located three-page appendix, expressly cross-referenced by paragraphs 14, 15 and 18. Part A covers provider experience, technical and legal risks, continuity, privacy and AML/CFT; Part B adds custody considerations for bearer-form Tokenised Securities using permissionless tokens on public-permissionless networks. Describing the appendix as outside the main retained body is a document-location inference supported by the packet structure; describing it as unavailable in this packet is incorrect. The legislative-authority gap remains. The circular references SFO Schedule 1 definitions, SFO Part IV, the Cap. 32 prospectus regime and AMLO section 53ZRA, but does not supply their complete operative texts or establish an exhaustive list of applicable provisions. The prior proposals are consistent on this central distinction; the exception-focused qualifications prevent overstating the appendix's scope or treating conditional regulatory relief as general permission. Official authenticity, relevant-date currentness and transaction-specific application remain unestablished. This is a source-answer proposal, not legal proof.
